Discretize a Time Series into States

Source: R/discretize.R
discretize.Rd

discretize() exposes every internal state discretizer as a first-class verb. It accepts the same inputs as tsn() (plus a tsn object) and returns a tidy one-row-per-observation table of discretized states. tsn() routes its own state aggregation through the same engine, so tsn(x, "<method>") and discretize(x, method = "<method>") produce identical state assignments. Scalar methods learn one shared state space from all selected values. Temporal methods ("ordinal", "adaptive_magnitude", and "dtw") first compute patterns or windows within each series, never across an ID boundary, and then use a shared alphabet or clustering model.

Usage

discretize(
  data,
  value = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  series = NULL,
  method = "quantile",
  n_states = 3L,
  breaks = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  transform = "none",
  m = NULL,
  tau = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A numeric vector, ts, matrix, named list of numeric vectors, data frame, or a tsn object (its source series are used, so value, id, and time cannot be supplied with it). Missing or non-finite values are an error rather than being dropped or kept as an NA state; remove them first, for example with subset().

value

Optional value-column name for long data.

id

Optional series-ID column name for long data.

time

Optional time-column name for long data.

series

Optional series IDs or wide-data column names to select.

method

Discretization method. One of "threshold", "width", "quantile", "kde", "kmeans", "gaussian", "hclust", "ordinal", "symbolic", "change_points", "entropy", "magnitude", "adaptive_magnitude", "percentile_magnitude", or "dtw".

n_states

Number of states requested. Not consumed by "ordinal", whose state count follows the embedding arguments m and tau; supplying both is an error. Bins that receive no observation are dropped (with a tsn_state_shortfall warning), so the realized count (reported in the printed header) can be smaller, for example with "threshold" breaks that leave a bin empty, an empty middle "width" bin, or a "dtw" cluster that wins no observation's vote.

breaks

Interior thresholds for method = "threshold", which requires them: finite values strictly inside the data range. When n_states is not supplied it is set to length(breaks) + 1; an explicit n_states must equal that. An error with any other method, which computes its own boundaries.

labels

Optional custom state labels: unique, non-missing, non-empty strings, one per realized state (in increasing state order). When NULL, states are numbered consecutively.

transform

Pre-discretization transform: "none" (default), "log" (uses log1p(abs(x))), or "zscore" (standardized values).

m

Embedding dimension for method = "ordinal" (default 3). An error with any other method.

tau

Embedding lag for method = "ordinal" (default 1). An error with any other method.

seed

Optional seed for the stochastic discretizers ("kmeans" and "gaussian"). An error with the deterministic methods.

Value

A tidy data frame of class tsn_states, one row per observation, with columns id (character), time, value, state (a factor whose levels are the realized states in increasing order), and probability (the assignment confidence; 1 for hard assignments). Rows are grouped by series in order of first appearance and, when time is supplied, sorted by it within each series. time is the supplied time column for long data with time and the series time for a ts; otherwise it numbers the observations within each series (long data with id only, named lists) or is the row index (vectors, matrices, wide data frames). The discretization model and any bin boundaries are stored in the model and breaks attributes.

References

Bandt, C., & Pompe, B. (2002). Permutation entropy: A natural complexity measure for time series. Physical Review Letters, 88, 174102. doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.88.174102

Examples

discretize(c(1, 5, 2, 9, 3, 7, 4, 8), method = "quantile", n_states = 3)
#> <tsn_states> quantile discretization (transform: none): 8 observations, 3 states
#>        id time value state probability
#>  series_1    1     1     1           1
#>  series_1    2     5     2           1
#>  series_1    3     2     1           1
#>  series_1    4     9     3           1
#>  series_1    5     3     1           1
#>  series_1    6     7     3           1
#>  series_1    7     4     2           1
#>  series_1    8     8     3           1

discretize(
  c(1, 5, 2, 9, 3, 7, 4, 8),
  method = "quantile",
  n_states = 3,
  labels = c("low", "mid", "high")
)
#> <tsn_states> quantile discretization (transform: none): 8 observations, 3 states
#>        id time value state probability
#>  series_1    1     1   low           1
#>  series_1    2     5   mid           1
#>  series_1    3     2   low           1
#>  series_1    4     9  high           1
#>  series_1    5     3   low           1
#>  series_1    6     7  high           1
#>  series_1    7     4   mid           1
#>  series_1    8     8  high           1

discretize(c(3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6), method = "ordinal", m = 3)
#> <tsn_states> ordinal discretization (transform: none): 8 observations, 5 states
#>        id time value state probability
#>  series_1    1     3     3           1
#>  series_1    2     1     2           1
#>  series_1    3     4     3           1
#>  series_1    4     1     1           1
#>  series_1    5     5     4           1
#>  series_1    6     9     5           1
#>  series_1    7     2     5           1
#>  series_1    8     6     5           1

discretize(c(10, 12, 8, 25, 40, 44, 9), method = "width", transform = "log")
#> <tsn_states> width discretization (transform: log): 7 observations, 3 states
#>        id time value state probability
#>  series_1    1    10     1           1
#>  series_1    2    12     1           1
#>  series_1    3     8     1           1
#>  series_1    4    25     2           1
#>  series_1    5    40     3           1
#>  series_1    6    44     3           1
#>  series_1    7     9     1           1
